title: Scene Describe Run
description: Async scene describe-run status payload. Submitted via POST /scene/describe/run as multipart/form-data: form fields 'tenant_id' (uuid), 'media_ids' (JSON int array), optional 'recognition_enabled' (boolean, default true), and optional 'idempotency_key' (16..128 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-]). Plus one file part 'image_<media_id>' (raw bytes) per media id. When recognition_enabled is false, the run writes alt text without identity fusion. An idempotency_key is deduped per (tenant_id, key): a replay returns 202 with the original run_id and starts no new work, while the same key with a different payload returns 409 'idempotency_conflict'. A present-but-malformed key returns 422. The key binds exactly two things: the SET of media_ids and recognition_enabled. Order and duplicates in media_ids are not part of the binding, so [70,71] and [71,70] under one key are the same submission and replay rather than conflict. Image bytes are NOT part of the binding: reusing one key for different bytes under the same media_id replays the first run and is caller error - the caller owns byte stability and must mint a new key when an asset's bytes change. The 409 body carries only 'code', 'message' and 'field'; it never discloses the reserved run's id or media_ids. A key held by a run that ends terminal with zero completed items (failed, cancelled, or completed_with_errors where every item failed) is released and may be re-reserved by a later submit; a key held by a run with at least one completed item is not, and has no TTL.

eta_seconds.description: Estimated seconds remaining; null unless the run is in-flight with measured progress.

gpu_state.description: Burst-GPU execution state read from the lifecycle snapshot /run/acx/gpu-state.json (single writer: infra.oci.gpu_lifecycle). 'unknown' when the snapshot is missing, unreadable, or stale — never fabricated as ready. See docs/workbay/contracts/gpu-lifecycle.md § GPU state snapshot.

recognition_enabled.description: Snapshot of WP acx_recognition_enabled at submit. When false, Describe writes alt text without identities. Defaults to true when omitted on submit.

deadline_seconds.description: Additive optional. The server's own end-to-end GENERATION budget for this whole accepted run: the budget the worker actually enforces, summed across the run's items. It explicitly does NOT include GPU warm-up / cold-start - the client adds the warm-up leg itself. Derived at accept from the per-item generation timeout the worker is handed (which depends on the active adapter, not on ACX_DESCRIPTION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS alone) multiplied by the run's unique item count, and snapshotted per run: a later config change does not move an accepted run's deadline. Null only for runs not created through POST /scene/describe/run.
